desc:
PrestaShop SEO and speed optimization makes your pages load faster and gives search engines a cleaner picture of your shop. Ecom Swift LLC tunes caching and images, fixes titles and URLs, resolves duplicates and reports before and after results.

## What does PrestaShop SEO and speed optimization involve?

It covers two linked jobs. The speed side reduces how long pages take to appear: caching, image sizes, scripts, module weight and database load. The search side makes sure each page has a clear title, description and address, that duplicate pages do not compete with each other, and that your sitemap and redirects are in order.

Both jobs aim at the same person, a shopper arriving from a search result who wants to see a product quickly and trust what they find.

## Why slow and messy shops lose visitors

A PrestaShop store can gain weight over the years. Each module may add scripts and styles, each product may carry full-size photos, and each filter or combination may create another address for the same content. The result is slow category pages, repeated pages that confuse search engines and titles that say little about the product.

Visitors rarely wait for a slow page, and search engines struggle to decide which of several similar pages deserves to appear. Both problems are quiet, so shops live with them for a long time.

## How speed and search work improve results

Faster pages help in two ways. Shoppers stay longer and reach the cart more often when pages respond quickly, and search engines treat page experience as one of many signals. Cleaner titles and descriptions help people decide to click a result. Clean URLs and fewer duplicate pages let search engines understand which page matters for each product or category.

We cannot promise rankings, because many factors outside the shop, such as competitors and links, play a part. What we deliver is a measurable technical improvement, shown in a before and after summary.

## What strong PrestaShop optimization includes

- A speed test of your key pages before any change is made.
- Smarty template caching and CCC settings (combine, compress, cache) tuned for your shop.
- Images compressed and sized correctly, with modern formats as an option.
- A review of modules that add weight, with slow ones replaced or removed.
- Product and category pages given their own titles and meta descriptions.
- Friendly URLs checked and redirects set for changed addresses.
- Duplicate product and category page problems resolved with proper settings.
- 404 errors found and cleaned up.
- XML sitemap and robots settings checked.
- Product markup that can support rich results.
- Database and cache table cleanup in the larger package.
- A keyword map linking main categories to the phrases shoppers use.

## How we work

We test your key pages first and record the starting results. Then we change settings on a safe copy where a change could affect the layout, and apply them to the live shop once tested. After each round we measure again.

The Basic package tunes caching, compresses images on key pages and checks friendly URLs and the sitemap. Standard adds a review of slow modules, written titles and descriptions for a batch of pages, duplicate page fixes and redirect and 404 cleanup. Premium adds database cleanup, more titles and descriptions, product markup and a keyword map for your main categories.

We write titles and descriptions. We do not write full product descriptions as part of this service.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Keep backups before touching caching or database settings.
- Resize photos before uploading them.
- Write titles that say what the page sells, in natural words.
- Use redirects when an address changes.
- Test again after every new module is installed.

**Avoid:**
- Stuffing titles with repeated keywords.
- Turning on every cache option without testing checkout.
- Leaving old products live as empty pages.
- Judging speed from one test on one page.
- Removing modules without checking what they control.

## Who this is for

This service suits shops whose category pages feel slow, especially on phones. It suits owners who see several addresses for the same product in search results. It also suits sellers who added many modules over time and want to know which ones cost speed.

## How to get started

Send us your shop address and the pages that matter most. Give us staff or developer access, and, if you have it, access to your Search Console and analytics as a team user. We never need your passwords. We reply with a short checklist, record the starting results and begin the work.
